claim: Sepilok Nature Resort has air-con wooden twin chalets around a natural lake, gardens with 150+ orchid species, minutes' walk to the Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre, and wild orangutans/pythons wandering among the chalets.
quote: it is actually not uncommon to have Orang Utans or pythons wandering around among the chalets ... The Orang-Utan Rehabilitation Center ... are just a few minutes' walk away.

claim: Sepilok Nature Lodge (formerly Nature Resort) is a tranquil lakeside hideaway with bungalows in dense foliage; villas described as beautiful and quite luxurious, guests see orangutans near accommodation.
quote: Villas are described as beautiful and quite luxurious, with guests reporting to see orangutans near their accommodations.

claim: Sepilok Forest Edge Resort offers village-style chalets on lawns with wildlife-attracting fruit trees (broadbills, kingfishers, pittas, occasional orangutans) plus the Labuk B&B longhouse dorms.
quote: the resort features bungalows ... The longhouse-style wooden building hosts an excellent hostel (Labuk B&B) ... orangutans occasionally stopping by the fruit trees.

claim: Forest Edge Resort is a 15-min walk to the Orangutan Centre; dorms ~US$20 and private rooms ~US$120, with bungalows seen as pricey but the charm and cleanliness praised.
quote: dorms starting from ~$20 USD and private rooms from $120 USD ... the bungalows were thought overpriced.

claim: Paganakan Dii sits on a forested ridge 5 km from Sepilok with a free shuttle; reviews are mixed — lovely setting and cheap meals, but some chalets run hot with the occasional critter.
quote: Perched on a narrow forested ridge ... free shuttle to the Orangutan and Sun Bear Centres ... others report their rooms were hot and stuffy.

claim: Paganakan Dii's ridge chalets are minimalist, sleek and thoughtfully designed, with a stilted longhouse dorm whose slatted mosquito-screened walls open to the jungle breeze.
quote: The ridge chalet rooms are really well designed: minimalist, sleek, thoughtful. A stilted wooden longhouse houses the fan-cooled dorms and is open to the jungle breeze.

claim: Sepilok Jungle Resort has pretty grounds and a lake but recent reviews flag a tired pool and basic, somewhat overpriced rooms; Sepilok Nature Resort is the more modern sibling.
quote: The pool area has been criticized for looking tired with broken sun loungers and murky water ... Rooms are basic but somewhat overpriced.

claim: Paganakan Dii online room rates start around US$23 for a mid-June 2026 stay.
quote: Online room rates at Paganakan Dii Tropical Retreat start at US$23 for a stay in mid-June 2026.

claim: Sukau Rainforest Lodge is an award-winning eco-lodge on the Kinabatangan with villa and deluxe rooms, sustainability programs and packages roughly RM 2,650–10,770 (3D2N villa ~RM 3,955).
quote: Tours range from RM 2,650–RM 10,770 ... the most popular being the 'Kinabatangan Wildlife Safari (Villa)' at RM 3,955 for 3D2N.

claim: Sukau Rainforest Lodge is ranked #1 specialty lodging in Kinabatangan District, with a 500m covered Hornbill Boardwalk, 20 new villas plus 20 superior rooms and two pools.
quote: the Hornbill Boardwalk – the elevated and covered walkway stretching in a 500m loop ... 20 brand new Villas in addition to 20 Superior rooms. Amenities include two pools.

claim: The Last Frontier Resort sits atop a 100m hill by the Kinabatangan, reached by ~600 steps, all-inclusive with 3 meals and an evening river cruise.
quote: located on top of a 100 meter high hill ... accessible only via a 600-step staircase ... Packages include accommodation, 3 meals a day and an evening river cruise.

claim: The Last Frontier has just 4 guestrooms; couples rate it ~9.8 and praise food as among the best in Malaysia, with ridge views as far as Sandakan on clear days.
quote: The resort has 4 guestrooms ... they rated it 9.8 for a two-person trip ... Food is some of the best guests have eaten in Malaysia.

claim: Bilit Rainforest Lodge is a riverside lodge on the Bilit stretch of the Kinabatangan offering river cruises and combo packages including Selingan Turtle Island.
quote: 3D2N Selingan Turtle Island & Bilit Rainforest Lodge

claim: On the Kinabatangan, Bilit is narrower upriver with animals close to the boat, while Abai in the lower river is wider, quieter and more remote; Sukau gives access and variety.
quote: Bilit is located further upriver, where the river becomes narrower ... animals often closer to the boat ... Abai offers isolation, Sukau provides access and variety, and Bilit delivers closer encounters.

claim: Abai Jungle Lodge is built fully on stilts with wooden walkways, near a traditional fishing village in the quieter lower Kinabatangan, reached by a ~1-hr boat ride from Sandakan.
quote: fully built on stilts, with wooden walkways connecting rooms ... reached by a scenic one-hour boat ride from Sandakan jetty or Sukau.

claim: Borneo Nature Lodge is an eco-resort on the Kinabatangan with jungle gardens and daily wildlife at the door, though a 2026 review notes some areas feeling neglected and due a refresh.
quote: an eco-friendly resort ... the location and gardens were lovely, but public and private areas felt neglected, needing a deep clean and refresh.

claim: Kinabatangan Riverside Lodge (run by SI Tours) has comfortable rooms, good food and a pool, with multi-day packages departing Sandakan by boat along the coast into the river.
quote: comfortable rooms and a nice pool ... run by SI Tours ... packages that depart from Sandakan by boat along the coast and then into the river.

claim: Sukau Greenview Lodge sits in Sukau village on the riverfront with basic but clean rooms, a riverview communal area and good value.
quote: located right in Sukau Village, directly on the riverfront ... fairly basic, but guests spend very little time in the room ... excellent value for money.

claim: Sukau Greenview Lodge is a locally owned eco-lodge founded by Mr Jamaluddin Lias, started as a B&B in 2008 and expanded since.
quote: an eco-lodge owned and operated by locals from Sukau village. Founded by Mr Jamaluddin Lias, it started as a B&B in 2008.

claim: Nature Lodge Kinabatangan at Bilit has rebranded to Tanini Kinabatangan and remains very basic.
quote: now known as Tanini Kinabatangan (Formerly Nature Lodge Kinabatangan) ... rooms are extremely basic.

claim: Birders compare the Kinabatangan sub-zones Bilit, Sukau and Abai for lodge choice and wildlife access.
quote: Kinabatangan: Bilit, Sukau or Abai?

claim: Selingan Turtle Island has 25 air-con rooms with twin beds and private bathrooms but no hot water, no porters (carry bags ~600m from the boat) and buffet cafeteria meals.
quote: 25 air-conditioned guestrooms ... Hot water is not available. The chalets are located approximately 600 meters from the beach ... no porters on the island.

claim: Selingan Turtle Island, 40 km north of Sandakan in the Sulu Sea, offers a rare chance to witness turtles nesting at night; beds are limited so booking ahead is needed.
quote: Selingan Island is located 40 km north of Sandakan ... a rare chance to witness turtles nesting at night.

claim: There is one join-in boat to Selingan daily at 10:00 (be in Sandakan by 09:00); a ranger leads guests to watch turtles lay eggs, egg collection to the hatchery and hatchling release.
quote: only 1 join-in boat transfer to Selingan Island daily at 10:00AM ... a Park Ranger will inform you on the right time to encounter turtles laying their eggs.

claim: Effective 1 January 2026 single-use plastic bags are prohibited in all Sabah Parks; visitors must bring reusable bags.
quote: Effective 1 January 2026, the use of single-use plastic bags is strictly prohibited in all Sabah Parks ... bring their own reusable eco bags.

claim: A 2D1N Selingan Turtle Island package is priced around MYR 1,380 per person.
quote: Selingan Turtle Island - MYR 1,380

claim: NAK Hotel is Sandakan's oldest purpose-built hotel, family-run since 1966, with a quirky lobby of oxblood walls, Chinese lanterns, birdcages and Oriental vases.
quote: the oldest, purpose-built hotel in Sandakan ... family run since 1966 ... oxblood walls, Chinese lanterns, giant bird cages and Oriental vases.

claim: NAK Hotel's rooftop Balin Roof Garden Bar & Bistro is built around a giant water tank with breathtaking views over Sandakan city and the Sulu Sea.
quote: a rooftop garden bar and restaurant which features breathtaking views ... built around and on top of a giant water tank.

claim: Sabah Hotel Sandakan is a 4-star resort set amid tropical rainforest with colonial-feel rooms and a large free-form pool with water slides.
quote: 4-star deluxe luxuries nestled amidst one of the world's last natural tropical rainforests ... a large free-form swimming pool complete with water slides.

claim: Sabah Hotel gives easy orangutan/sun-bear/proboscis access without a jungle lodge, but it is ~1.5 km from town (taxi/Grab) and some rooms feel dated.
quote: easy access to experiences with orangutans, sun bears and proboscis monkeys ... about 1 mile down the hill ... the decor feels dated.

claim: The English Tea House serves fine teas, scones and clotted cream in a colonial setting overlooking Sandakan Bay on the Heritage Trail; it is a restaurant, not lodging.
quote: scones & clotted cream, delicious cakes & pastries ... spectacular views of the town and Sandakan Bay.

claim: The English Tea House occupies a restored colonial house beside the Agnes Keith House museum on Jalan Istana, with 1.5 acres of manicured lawns and a croquet lawn.
quote: housed in a meticulously renovated colonial house surrounded by 1.5 acres of perfectly manicured lawns ... beside the iconic Agnes Keith House.

claim: Hotel Sandakan is central with large rooms, a 5-min walk to the waterfront and onto the Heritage Trail.
quote: strategically located at town centre ... within walking distance to ... Sandakan Heritage Trails ... only a quick 5 minute walk to the waterfront.

claim: Four Points by Sheraton Sandakan is a 299-room waterfront chain hotel on Harbour Square with a pool, but reviews are mixed and some flag it needing refurbishment.
quote: right on a scenic waterfront pedestrian promenade ... 299 rooms ... the hotel needing thorough refurbishment, with very dirty windows and torn bedding.

claim: The best months to visit Sandakan are the drier March–September, with May–September fruiting bringing orangutans closer to the ground; November–December are heaviest NE-monsoon rain.
quote: the dry season from March to September is generally considered the best time ... May to September is particularly ideal, as trees fruit at this time ... avoid November and December.

claim: The Oct–Feb wet season swells the Kinabatangan and triggers fruiting that draws abundant wildlife to the riverbanks, making it strong for river wildlife despite the rain.
quote: the wet season from October to February is often considered the ultimate time for wildlife encounters, as the increased rainfall swells the rivers.

claim: Peak wildlife activity in places like Kinabatangan tends to fall between May and August when fruiting trees draw animals out.
quote: Peak wildlife activity tends to occur between May and August, especially in places like Kinabatangan, when fruiting trees draw animals out.

claim: Sepilok has far fewer beds than Sandakan town and private rooms are steeper there; some travellers base in town where rooms are cheaper, but Sepilok puts you on the orangutans' doorstep.
quote: Sepilok doesn't offer as many accommodation options as Sandakan ... private rooms in Sepilok are steep, which is why some prefer staying in Sandakan instead.

claim: Practical first-visit guidance on reaching and basing in Sandakan and Sepilok, including booking jungle lodges ahead in high season.
quote: Best Things to Do & How to Get to Sepilok & Sandakan [2026]

claim: Overview of the best Kinabatangan riverside lodges across Sukau, Bilit and Abai for choosing a river base.
quote: Kinabatangan River Accommodation: My Best 7 Riverside Lodges in Borneo
